name: reply-drafter-rust
description: Drafts your reply to a message you received, in your own voice. Paste the incoming email, chat or text message, say what you want to say back ("say yes but not before Thursday", "decline politely") and paste 1-3 of your past replies: it measures your style from them (length, greeting, sign-off, contractions, exclamation marks, emoji) and checks the reply against those numbers. You get the reply, a shorter alternative and notes on how the tone was matched. It never invents a fact: anything specific you didn't give it becomes a placeholder like [date?], and it never accepts, declines or promises more than you said. Revisions ("shorter", "say no instead") work on what is still in the recent conversation; it keeps nothing between messages, so a long message or past replies from earlier may need to be pasted again. It only drafts and sends nothing. For a new message with nothing to reply to, use the drafter. Not for answering questions, essays, code or translation. This is the Rust build: the same reply drafter as a small native binary.

skills.name: Draft a reply in your tone
skills.description: A reply to a pasted email, chat or text message, written in the style measured from your past replies, with a shorter alternative and tone notes; missing specifics become placeholders. Revise it on request while it is still in the recent conversation. Draft only: nothing is sent.
examples: Reply to this email: <paste> My past replies: <1-3 examples>. Say yes but not before Thursday.
Reply to this Slack message: <paste>, decline politely
